# Write: Airway case study

## Create your report

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/create_report.R airway
```

Open `reports/airway-report.qmd`. The helper creates a separate Quarto project inside ignored `reports/` and preserves existing writing. The tracked starter lives in `templates/report.qmd`. Follow [Write the report](../../02-write-the-report.qmd) for the shared structure.

## Turn the checks into evidence

Cite Himes et al. (2014), DOI [10.1371/journal.pone.0099625](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0099625), and the airway package. State that eight samples represent four matched cell lines and that the fitted contrast is treated relative to untreated, accounting for cell line.

For the supplied reference input, SRR1039508 has 20,637,971 supplied counts and 24,633 detected genes; report these only after your own verification. Add one gene's actual estimate, uncertainty and adjusted evidence, together with six figure observations. A small adjusted p-value does not establish a mechanism or clinical benefit. Preserve that interpretation boundary.

## Render and review

From the main project folder:

```bash
cd reports
quarto render airway-report.qmd
cd ..
```

Read `reports/airway-report.html`. The starter links all six figures in `../results/airway/figures/` and embeds them in the rendered HTML. Confirm they display, remove bracketed starter text and trace every number to a table or calculation. Existing older reports are not rewritten automatically; update their image paths and rendering configuration as needed.

**Your task:** identify one statement supported by an independent calculation, one by the fitted model, and one describing a limitation. State how AI helped and what you checked yourself.

Keep generated reports and HTML in ignored `reports/`, separate from book chapters. Inspect content for private data before sharing.
